question: A quadratic equation whose roots are - (2)/(3) and - (3)/(2).
solution:
**Given:**

Roots of the equation = - (2)/(3) and - (3)/(2)

**Concept used:**

For an equation ax² + bx + c = 0,

Roots: x = p, x = q which means x - p = 0 and x - q = 0

When multiply these two equations, we will get the quadratic equation (x - p)(x - q)

**Calculation:**

Roots,

 x = - (2)/(3)\ x + {2over 3} = 0 

and 

 x = - (3)/(2)\ x +{3 over 2} = 0

Multiplying these two to get the quadratic equation, 

( x + {2over 3} ) ( x + {3over 2} ) =0\ x² + {2 over 3}x + {3 over 2}x +1 =0 \ x² +( {4x +9x over6}) +1=0\ x² + {13x over 6}+1 =0\ 6x² + 13x+6 = 0

**Hence, the quadratic equation is 6x2 + 13x + 6 = 0.**
